name: KirbyBase
tagline: Tiny pure-Ruby and pure-Python DBMS that stores tables as plain-text files.
description: KirbyBase is Jamey Cribbs's small database management system, written once in pure Python and again in pure Ruby, that keeps each table as a human-readable delimited text file. You define typed fields, then insert, update and select records; the Ruby version uses code blocks as query predicates, supports lookups and links between tables, computed fields and indexes, and can run embedded in a script or as a simple client-server process. It was popular in the mid-2000s Ruby scene for scripts and small apps that wanted structure without SQLite. The last Ruby gem (2.6.1) dates from 2012 and the Python package stopped at 1.9; the original netpromi.com site is gone.
statusNote: No releases since the 2.6.1 Ruby gem (2012); original site offline. Use SQLite or a small JSON store instead.

scale.notes: Plain-text files; fine for thousands of records, slow beyond that.

strengths: Data files are plain text you can read and edit by hand
Pure Ruby/Python with no native dependencies
Ruby blocks as query predicates feel natural in scripts
weaknesses: No transactions or crash safety; whole-file rewrites
Performance falls off quickly as tables grow
useCases: Legacy Ruby or Python scripts already using it
Teaching what a minimal DBMS needs
notIdealFor: Any dataset beyond a few megabytes
